answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a harbor pilot registry: each newcomer earns a jade seal before trading. First, it posts a $400 bond locked 90 days. Second, it completes 30 supervised jobs, each countersigned by a pilot. Third, auditors re-run a random 10% and slash the bond on mismatch. A pearl rating then grows only from audited work, never self-declared volume. Forging 1,000 fake pilots costs $400,000 in bonds plus 30,000 supervised hours; an honest pilot needs one bond. Like a harbor admitting only captains who have steered its channel, identity is earned, not printed.
